case.case_title: Ansalin Fernando v. Sarath Perera, Officer-in-Charge, Police Station, Chilaw and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 18/87, decided on 19 and 30 March 1990

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention and treatment of the 6th respondent amounted to unlawful punishment in violation of Article 13(4).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the 6th respondent was subjected to degrading treatment and unlawful detention amounting to punishment without trial.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents did not specifically justify the treatment or detention as lawful punishment.
key_facts: The 6th respondent was detained for 49 days without lawful authority.
He was subjected to assaults, humiliation, blindfolding, chaining to a bench causing pain.
He was taken to a lonely house and assaulted during interrogation.
No lawful detention order covered the entire period of detention.
The treatment and detention were degrading and amounted to punishment without trial.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(4) prohibits punishment except by a competent court and clarifies that detention before trial is not punishment. The court held that unlawful detention accompanied by degrading treatment amounts to unlawful punishment violating Article 13(4).
reasoning.application_to_facts: The 6th respondent's prolonged unlawful detention and degrading treatment including chaining and assault constituted degrading treatment or punishment in violation of Article 13(4).
principles_established: Punishment must be imposed only by a competent court.
Detention before trial is not punishment but unlawful detention with degrading treatment can amount to unlawful punishment.
Degrading treatment during detention violates constitutional protections.
precedents_cited: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera (1985) 1 Sri LR 375

outcome.holding: The court held that the unlawful detention and degrading treatment of the 6th respondent violated Article 13(4) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation and costs were awarded to the petitioner on behalf of the 6th respondent.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) was central to the court's finding that the unlawful detention and degrading treatment amounted to unlawful punishment, supporting the relief granted.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the 6th respondent was detained unlawfully for 49 days and subjected to assaults, humiliation, blindfolding, and chaining, amounting to degrading treatment violating Article 13(4).
